h1: Employment contracts and probation terms for brewery staff
title: Brewery Staff Contracts and Probation | Craft Beer School
desc: What to put in brewery employment contracts in India: appointment letters, probation, notice, confidentiality, statutory benefits and safety duties.
teaser: A handshake hire works until the first disagreement. A clear contract makes that disagreement short.
standfirst: Breweries often hire their first people informally and pay for it later. A written appointment letter with clear probation terms costs little and settles most arguments before they start. Here is what we would put in one, with a lawyer checking the final version.
sections: Every employee needs a written letter

Every person you hire, from head brewer to dishwasher, should get a written appointment letter or employment contract before their first day. It should state the job title, start date, place of work, salary and how it is paid, working hours, leave, probation, notice period and who they report to.

State laws, usually through the local Shops and Establishments Act or the Factories Act for manufacturing sites, set rules on hours, overtime, weekly offs and leave. A production brewery and a brewpub may fall under different rules. Labour law in India varies by state and is changing, so have a local employment lawyer review your template once.
Probation: long enough to learn, short enough to be fair

Probation lets both sides check the fit. In India, three to six months is common. For brewery roles, three months suits bar, floor and kitchen staff, who show their quality quickly. Six months suits brewers, since you want to see them through several batches, at least one problem fermentation and a cleaning audit.

Write what happens at the end. Probation should end with a short review, a written confirmation or a written extension with reasons. Silence leaves everyone unsure. Many employers set a shorter notice period during probation, such as one or two weeks, with a longer one after confirmation, such as one month.

Set out the salary structure clearly: basic pay, allowances and any service charge share or incentive, with how it is calculated. Mention statutory benefits that apply. Provident fund usually applies once an establishment has 20 or more employees. Employees' State Insurance applies to establishments with 10 or more employees in covered areas, for staff earning up to ₹21,000 a month.

Thresholds and rates change, so check the current rules with your accountant before you write numbers into a contract. Pay salaries on a fixed date every month. Late pay is the fastest way to lose good people. Our guide to writing a brewery business plan shows where these costs belong in the plan.
Hours and shifts in a business that runs late

Brewpubs work evenings, weekends and festivals. Brewers start early on brew days, since a 500 litre brew often runs eight to ten hours from mash in to clean kit. The contract should state normal hours, the weekly off and how overtime or late closes are handled, within your state's rules.

Be honest about peak periods. If staff cannot take leave in the weeks around major festivals or New Year, say so in writing. People accept tough rosters they were told about. They resent ones that appear without warning.

Add a confidentiality clause covering recipes, process notes, supplier terms and sales data. It is reasonable and enforceable in a way that a broad non-compete usually is not, since Indian contract law generally does not uphold restrictions on working for a rival after employment ends.

Include the duties specific to a brewery: following safety procedures, wearing protective equipment when handling caustic or acid, never entering a tank without a confined space procedure and following the staff drinking policy. Link these to your staff handbook so the contract stays short and the detail stays current.

State how either side can end the contract: the notice period, payment in lieu of notice and what counts as serious misconduct that allows immediate termination after a fair process. For breweries, serious misconduct usually includes theft of stock, coming to work intoxicated, deliberately breaking safety rules and falsifying excise or quality records.

Write down the exit steps too: return of keys and uniforms, handover of logs and passwords and the final settlement date. Follow your own process every time. Inconsistent treatment is what turns a resignation into a dispute.

A few contract problems come up again and again in small breweries. Offer letters that promise a role and pay but say nothing about probation or notice. Salary paid partly in cash, which causes trouble at audits and when the employee needs a loan. Job titles that do not match the work, such as a head brewer who is really an assistant. Service charge or incentive schemes described verbally, then disputed when the numbers turn out lower than expected.

Each of these is easy to fix in the template. Put everything that affects pay or job security in writing. If a term changes later, issue a dated letter rather than relying on a WhatsApp message. Consistency matters as much as content: two people doing the same job on very different terms will find out within a month.

Keep a file for each employee with the signed appointment letter, ID and address proof, probation review, any warnings and leave records. Labour inspectors can ask for these. Your accountant needs them for statutory filings.

Contracts, probation and payroll are one part of running a brewery team well. Fitting them into a budget, a roster and a growth plan is the bigger skill.

Your first step: draft one appointment letter template this week and send it to a local employment lawyer for review.
faqs: How long should probation be for brewery staff in India?
Three to six months is common. Three months suits bar and floor roles; six months lets you see a brewer through several batches.
Do brewery employees get provident fund?
Provident fund usually applies once an establishment has 20 or more employees. Thresholds and rules change, so check with your accountant.
Can I stop a brewer from working for a competitor?
Broad post-employment non-compete clauses are generally not enforced in India. Confidentiality clauses protecting recipes and data are more useful. Take legal advice.
